name: St. Augustine History Paddle
place: Anastasia Island State Park, St. Augustine
included: Tent camping (shared sites with electricity and water), catered meals, river maps and evening programs.
cabinsNote: Rentals: Burnham Guides (official outfitter), Mary, mary@burnhamguides.com, 305-240-0650. RV site supplement: email janice.a.hindson@gmail.com. Beach bungalows are booked with the park at 904-460-9111, at your own cost.

overview.title: Paddle the Historic Coast
overview.text: One base camp, a short stroll from the beach, and a different paddle each day: Salt Run, Princess Place Preserve, the Bridge of Lions and Castillo de San Marcos, the GTM Research Reserve and Fort Matanzas. Leave your tent up all week.
minis: Anastasia Island State Park, all week
Of pristine beach next to camp

days.title: Arrive at Anastasia Island
days.body: Check in from 3 to 5 PM and set up your tent at your shared campsite, which has electricity and water. Dinner is at 6 PM, followed by the trip overview and a talk from regional waterway advocates, then the campfire.

days.label: Days 2 to 5
days.title: Daily paddles on the Historic Coast
days.body: Breakfast at 7:30 AM, then a daily paddle highlighting the area. Depending on tide, weather and conditions, we return to base camp each evening. Dinner is at 6 PM, with a speaker or live music, then the campfire.

days.title: Breakfast and farewell
days.body: Breakfast at 7:30 AM, then strike camp. Tents and gear need to be down by 9:30 AM.

places: Launch from camp and paddle past the St. Augustine Lighthouse, dunes and narrow waterways. Roseate spoonbills feed here.
A Flagler County park with the oldest homestead in the county and a 1886 hunting lodge, where the Matanzas River meets Pellicer Creek.
Castillo de San Marcos and the Bridge of Lions
The oldest masonry fort in the continental United States, seen from the water.
Guana River and the GTM Research Reserve
Manatees, sometimes dolphins, and lots of birds on a stretch of the Intracoastal Waterway that is easy to overlook.
A coquina watchtower finished in 1742 to guard the southern approach to St. Augustine.
The last natural, undredged inlet on Florida’s Atlantic coast.
placesTitle: Some of the places we paddle

camps.name: Anastasia Island State Park
camps.note: Shared campsites with electricity and water, a short walk from the beach.

boat: Sit-in kayak, 14 feet or longer, with a rudder or skeg and a spray skirt. You should know how to swim and have solid kayaking, rescue and wet-exit skills.
baggage: Two bags and 40 pounds in total. You carry them from your car to camp and back at the end. Label them with your name.
water: Non-inflatable Coast Guard-approved PFD, worn on the water
Bow line, 8 to 10 ft, secured so it cannot come loose
Grab loops at bow and stern
First aid kit in a waterproof cover
Repair kit (duct tape, sealant, waterproof tape)
Rain gear and a fleece or light jacket
Dry change of clothes in a waterproof bag
Water for the day and snacks (lunch is provided)
land: Something to read, music or earplugs
faq: Dinner at 6 PM and an evening program at 7 PM. Programs include authors, historians and environmental experts, and one night of live music.
How do we get to the launches?
Paddlers self-shuttle to the launch each day.
Open to all skill levels. Paddlers under 18 must be with a parent or guardian, with no more than two children under 12 per adult. A signed waiver and emergency contact are required. No pets.
What are the rules on the water?
Wear a non-inflatable PFD at all times. People-powered boats only. Follow park rules, including the alcohol ban, and respect private property along the river.
All payments are non-refundable, including for weather and water levels. Paddle Florida strongly recommends buying trip cancellation insurance from an outside provider.
Yes. Final details are emailed 7 to 10 days before the trip.
